1.1: In the second year of King Darius, in the sixth month, on the first day, God dropped a word on Haggai for Zerubbabel (Shealtiel's son, the governor of Judah) and Joshua (Jehozadak's son, the high priest).
1.2: "The Lord of Heaven's Armies said: These folks out here keep sayin', 'It ain't time to rebuild the Lord's house yet.'"
1.3: Then God spoke again through Haggai:
1.4: "So let me get this straight—y'all got time to live comfy in your fancy houses, but My house still sittin' in ruins?"
1.5: Listen up—this what the Lord of Hosts says: "Check yourself. Look at how you've been livin'."
1.6: "Y'all plantin' seeds but barely harvestin'. You eat, but you still hungry. You drink, but it don't quench your thirst. You get dressed, but still cold. You work hard for your money, But it's like puttin' it in a purse with holes in it."
1.7: The Lord of Hosts says it again: "Check yourself. Look at what you do."
1.8: "Go up to the mountains, bring back wood, and rebuild My house. Do that, and I'll be pleased—I'll be glorified," says the Lord.
1.9: "Y'all expected big results, but it all came up short. Even when you did bring stuff home, I blew it away. Wanna know why?" says the Lord of Hosts. "'Cause My house is still tore down, while y'all stay runnin' to take care of your own."
1.10: "That's why the skies hold back the rain and the ground won't grow nothin'."
1.11: "I'm the one who called that drought—on the land, the hills, the grain, the wine, the oil, on everything the earth produces. Even the people and animals feel it. I shut it all down—your hustle included."
1.12: Then Zerubbabel and Joshua, along with everybody left in Judah, actually listened to God and to Haggai, His prophet. When they realized God really sent this word, they got shook and humbled themselves.
1.13: Then Haggai gave 'em another word from the Lord: "I'm right here with y'all," says the Lord.
1.14: So God stirred up Zerubbabel, Joshua, and all the people. He lit a fire in their spirit—and they got to work on the house of the Lord of Hosts, their God.
1.15: This all went down on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, during the second year of King Darius.

2.1: In the seventh month, on the 21st day, God gave Haggai another word.
2.2: He told him, "Go talk to Zerubbabel (Shealtiel's son, governor of Judah), Joshua (Jehozadak's son, the high priest), and the rest of the people. Say this to 'em:
2.3: 'Who here remembers how the old temple used to look? Ain't this new one lookin' kinda… underwhelming compared to that?'
2.4: But God says, 'Zerubbabel, don't let that discourage you—be strong. Joshua, you too—be strong. And all y'all, the people of the land—be strong and get to work. I'm with you,' says the Lord of Hosts.
2.5: 'My Spirit is still with y'all just like I promised back when I brought y'all outta Egypt. So don't be scared!'
2.6: "This what the Lord of Hosts says: 'In just a little while, I'm gon' shake things up—heaven, earth, sea, and dry land.
2.7: I'm gon' shake up all the nations, and they gon' bring in what's most precious. And this temple? I'ma fill it with My glory,' says the Lord of Hosts.
2.9: And the glory of this new house? It's gon' outshine the old one. And in this place, I'm givin' peace,' says the Lord of Hosts."
2.10: On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, God came back with another word to Haggai:
2.12: 'If somebody's carrying holy meat in the fold of their robe and that robe touches some bread or stew or wine or oil—does that food become holy too?'" The priests answered, "Nah, it don't."
2.13: Then Haggai said, "What if somebody touches a dead body and then touches the food—does that food become unclean?" The priests said, "Yeah, it becomes unclean."
2.14: Then Haggai hit 'em with the truth: "That's exactly what y'all been like," says the Lord. "Y'all and everything y'all been doing—unclean. Even your offerings—unclean."
2.15: "Now pay attention to what happens from this day forward. Back when y'all hadn't laid even one stone for the temple,
2.16: y'all kept coming up short. You expected twenty measures—you got ten. You pressed for fifty baths of wine—you got twenty.
2.17: I sent blight, mildew, and hail to shut your hustle down. But still, y'all ain't turned back to Me," says the Lord.
2.18: "But from today on—the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the day the foundation got laid—I want y'all to take note.
2.19: The seeds ain't even come up yet—vine, fig, pomegranate, olive—ain't none of it produced. But from this day on, I'm gon' bless you."
2.20: That same day, God gave Haggai another word:
2.22: 'I'm about to shake up heaven and earth. I'm toppling thrones and smashing kingdoms.
2.23: I'm tearing down the enemy's war machines—their chariots, their horses, and their riders. They gon' turn on each other with swords.'
2.24: 'And on that day,' says the Lord of Hosts, 'I'm choosin' you, Zerubbabel. I'm makin' you My signet ring—My chosen one,' says the Lord of Hosts."
